summary: Forensics feature tested end-to-end with live Etherscan data (3 scans total: Tornado Cash donation as admin, 0xab5801... as sender, deal recipient wallet via quick button as recipient in UI). Backend 16/16 pytest passed: 401 unauth on all 4 endpoints, 400 on invalid addresses, Tornado = Severe 100/100 with mixer exposure (self service + 8 TC counterparties + 1 OFAC-listed counterparty, wallet itself not OFAC-listed), normal wallet = Low 0/100 with real balance 16.69 ETH, persistence, list isolation (sender/recipient own only, admin all), cross-user GET/PDF 404, PDF valid (4 pages, contains exact title, no DEMO/SIMULATION watermark; only 'demo' is the requester email admin@vaultbridge.demo). UI: nav-forensics visible for admin/sender/recipient, invalid address toast shows backend message, report renders balance/risk/sanctions/activity/counterparties/tokens/recent tx with 20 etherscan tx links + 25 address links, history reopen works, PDF download works, quick sender/recipient buttons fill address + label and scan works. All core requirements pass; remaining items are accuracy/design issues.

minor.issue: 'Holdings' are computed as net of token transfers, not real token balances. For capped wallets this gives nonsense values (e.g. USDC net -2,194, '$ USDCFree.com - Visit to claim' net -536,320, MISTRAL AI net 48,110,850,768,482,940). Spam/airdrop phishing tokens are not filtered and rank first. The request asked for 'balance and holdings', and what is shown is misleading.

offset=10000 is requested, but Etherscan returned exactly 1000 records per category for 0xab5801 (normal/internal/token = 1000/1000/1000). history_capped uses >=1000, so the warning shows, but MAX_TX=10000 is misleading, and totals (eth_in 65,512 ETH) cover only the capped window.

If the GitHub OFAC download fails on a cold start, _ofac['set'] is empty and every wallet is reported 'not on the OFAC sanctions list' (list_size 0) with no error. The scan should fail or flag 'sanctions screening unavailable' when list_size == 0.

ui_bugs.issue: The tone() regex in common.jsx has no match for 'Severe risk', 'High risk', 'Low risk' or 'OFAC sanctioned', so these pills are neutral grey. A Severe band and an OFAC-sanctioned counterparty should be red and Low should be green. The BAND map in Forensics.jsx is defined but never used for the tone.

Mixer flags are shown as 'Rejected: Tornado Cash: Proxy'. 'Rejected:' is a hack to get a red colour and is semantically wrong. The pill should say e.g. 'Mixer: Tornado Cash: Proxy' and use a proper red tone.

issues: Very large net values wrap onto two lines in the 340px column (e.g. 'net 48,110,850,768,48 / 2,940')
Spam token names dominate the list
Long addresses break mid-string across lines in the mixer exposure and counterparties tables (e.g. '0x905b63...ec760' / '1')
The sidebar 'DEMO' badge next to ESCROW is still visible on the Forensics page, which is meant to be live data only (the report itself has no demo labels).

action_items: Add tone mappings for Severe/High (red), Medium (amber), Low (green) and 'OFAC sanctioned' (red) in StatusPill, or pass the BAND-mapped status. Replace the 'Rejected:' prefix on mixer flags.

Show real token holdings (e.g. account/tokenbalance per contract for the top tokens) or relabel the section as 'Token transfer activity (net of fetched transfers)'. Filter or flag spam tokens (names containing URLs or 'claim').
Fail or flag the scan when the OFAC list could not be loaded (list_size == 0) instead of silently reporting 'not on the OFAC list'.
Set MAX_TX to the effective provider cap (1000) or paginate, so history_capped is accurate.
Optional: wrap open(id) in Forensics.jsx in try/catch with an error toast (currently an unhandled promise rejection on failure).
critical_code_review_comments: forensics.load_ofac swallows HTTP errors and returns an empty set, so sanctions screening silently passes.
Forensics.jsx open() has no error handling; loadHistory has no catch.
Token net is computed from capped transfer windows, so it is not a holdings figure.
Counterparty sort key mixes ETH amounts and interaction counts (interactions/1000). Acceptable, but non-obvious.
Lazarus entries other than the Ronin exploiter (0x098b716b...) should be sourced or cited; unverified attribution in a due-diligence PDF is a liability.
